figures.headline: The architecture pairs a visual encoder with a language decoder and returns None for an absent car category.
citing_sentences: As shown in Figure 1, it couples a MoonViT-V2 (Kimi K3) visual encoder (Team et al., 2026) with a Qwen3-4B language decoder (Yang et al., 2025a).

figures.caption: Data engine. Multi-teacher fusion and task-specific validation guide expert iteration, with targeted observations resolving uncertain labels.
figures.headline: The data engine fuses multi-teacher annotations and validates them per task, with targeted observations resolving uncertain labels.
citing_sentences: Our data engine fuses multi-teacher annotations at the field level and applies task-specific validation (Figure 2).

figures.label: Figure 3
figures.caption: Overview of GroundingPI’s two-stage training pipeline. The first stage uses supervised fine-tuning (SFT) to learn structured grounding outputs with token-level cross-entropy. The second stage applies group relative policy optimization (GRPO) with task-specific rewards that balance grounding completeness and localization, and assess OCR text–geometry consistency and output reliability. Illustrative rollouts highlight common prediction errors and alternative OCR granularities.
figures.headline: The two-stage pipeline trains with token-level cross-entropy, then optimizes GRPO rewards for completeness, localization, and OCR consistency.
citing_sentences: To directly optimize localization, target coverage, and text–geometry consistency, we apply group relative policy optimization (GRPO) (Shao et al., 2024; Ping et al., 2026) with $G=8$ autoregressive responses per image–query pair (Figure 3).

abstract: Precise grounding matters. It specifies which object is the target and where that object is, even in clutter and for tiny objects, and it has to be fast enough for closed-loop control. Yet vision-language-action (VLA) and world-action models (WAMs) take perception from general-purpose vision-language and video-generation backbones, which still fail in these settings. We introduce GroundingPI, a 4B grounding foundation model that generates points and boxes as quantized coordinates in a shared vocabulary. Training combines multimodal and spatial pretraining, supervised fine-tuning, and reinforcement learning with GRPO, using supervision from public datasets and dedicated data engines. Against 44 baselines across 34 grounding benchmarks spanning 11 perceptual capabilities, GroundingPI establishes a new state of the art, averaging 73.68%, above the larger GPT-6 Astra (71.54%). As a downstream visual backbone, GroundingPI improves performance on robotic manipulation and autonomous driving. On RoboTwin 2.0, it outperforms every mainstream backbone we evaluate in all four out-of-distribution settings, by up to 24.8% relative to the strongest backbone. On RoboCasa-GR1, GroundingPI trained with 50% of the demonstrations outperforms those baselines trained with 75%. On nuScenes, used as the visual backbone, GroundingPI attains an average open-loop L2 error of 0.296 m. We systematically analyze GroundingPI’s pretraining in scale and data composition. Downstream autonomous driving and robotic manipulation improve as the pretraining is scaled. Analyzing the data recipe across these 11 perceptual capabilities shows dense grounding’s substantial benefits for both, and OCR’s potential as a catalyst for perceptual learning. These results support grounding as a perceptual foundation, and dedicated perceptual pretraining as a promising direction for foundation models of physical intelligence.

sections.body: The abstract argues that vision-language-action and world-action models take perception from general-purpose backbones that still fail at precise grounding in clutter and for tiny objects. It introduces GroundingPI, a grounding foundation model that generates points and boxes as quantized coordinates in a shared vocabulary. Training combines multimodal and spatial pretraining, supervised fine-tuning, and reinforcement learning with GRPO. The abstract reports that GroundingPI leads a large set of grounding baselines. It also reports improved performance as a visual backbone for robotic manipulation and autonomous driving, and that pretraining scale and data composition affect downstream results.

sections.body: The introduction argues that grounding is a core perceptual capability, and that vision-language-action and world-action models still build on general-purpose backbones not optimized for it. The authors' evaluations find substantial weaknesses in general-purpose vision-language models, especially on dense scenes and tiny objects, and room for improvement even in dedicated models such as Rex-Omni and LocateAnything. It proposes GroundingPI, a 4B-parameter grounding foundation model with a shared quantized-coordinate vocabulary, and reports 73.68% average versus 71.54% for GPT-6 Astra. Transfer results include up to 24.8% relative improvement on out-of-distribution robotic settings. The authors state that GPT-6 Astra still leaves room for improvement on demanding settings.
sections.heading: Introduction
sections.headline: Precise grounding is needed for physical intelligence, yet general-purpose backbones still fail on dense scenes and tiny objects.

sections.body: Related work covers three areas. Visual grounding models have moved from closed-set detection to language-conditioned localization and generative grounding that outputs labels and quantized coordinates. Physical-intelligence models inherit priors from VLMs and video models, but these broad capabilities do not necessarily give precise, task-conditioned perception. Perceptual learning for action transfer adds bounding-box prediction, affordance representations, or spatial auxiliary supervision to policies. The authors argue these approaches often depend on additional annotations or policy-specific components and are difficult to scale. This motivates a perception-native foundation model trained before action adaptation. No experiments are reported in this section.
sections.heading: Related Work
sections.headline: Prior grounding models and policy recipes add perception as task-specific proxies rather than a native foundation capability.

sections.body: GroundingPI pairs a MoonViT-V2 visual encoder with a Qwen3-4B language decoder. A projector aggregates adjacent 2×2 visual features and maps them to the language embedding space. Semantic labels, protocol markers, and 1,000 quantized coordinate tokens share one output vocabulary. Training has three parts. Base training aligns the projector and then updates all modules on multimodal and general visual data. Supervised fine-tuning minimizes token-level cross-entropy over assistant responses, protocol markers, and coordinates. Reinforcement post-training applies GRPO with G=8 autoregressive responses per image–query pair. For grounding, the reward combines set coverage with a strict score; for OCR, it uses Hungarian one-to-one matching. A data engine fuses multi-teacher annotations and validates each field.
sections.heading: GroundingPI: A Grounding Foundation Model
sections.headline: GroundingPI outputs boxes and points as quantized coordinates in one shared vocabulary, trained by fine-tuning and GRPO.

sections.body: Driving is evaluated on nuScenes as language-conditioned trajectory prediction. The front-camera image and historical ego states go in, and the future trajectory is written as six ordered waypoints at 0.5-second intervals over a three-second horizon, using the existing coordinate vocabulary. Manipulation follows a pi-style flow-matching policy, with intermediate features from the foundation injected into an Action DiT through cross-attention layers. The comparison fixes the action learner and varies only the pretrained foundation, across four model families: general-purpose vision-language models, video-generation backbones, grounding models, and embodied foundation models. Each benchmark keeps action data, optimization budget, and inference procedure fixed. This section describes the setup and does not report results.
sections.heading: GroundingPI Model towards Physical Intelligence
sections.headline: Transfer setup fixes the action learner and swaps only the perceptual backbone for driving and manipulation.

sections.body: GroundingPI is compared with 44 baselines on 34 benchmarks spanning 11 perceptual capabilities. Its results are means of ten runs; other baselines are averaged over three runs. Table 1 reports 74.53 on Dense200 against 65.04 for GPT-6 Astra and 14.02 for Qwen3-VL-4B, although VisDrone remains challenging. Table 2 shows GroundingPI improving over the selected compact baselines on all robot, spatial, and GUI benchmarks, while Astra retains a substantial advantage. Ablations show quantized coordinates raise the average from 71.21 to 73.68, and textual coordinates run at 0.25× the relative speed. Table 5 reports 7.6 tokens per box on COCO for GroundingPI versus 148.8 for SEED1.5-VL, a serialization measure rather than matched latency.
sections.heading: Experiments
sections.headline: GroundingPI averages 73.68% across 34 benchmarks, above GPT-6 Astra's 71.54%, but trails Astra on some tasks.

sections.body: The conclusion restates that GroundingPI, a 4B-parameter model, outperforms similarly sized models across 34 grounding benchmarks, remains competitive with GPT-6 Astra, and transfers to driving and manipulation. It argues that precise perception supports reliable System 1 execution, while broad reasoning serves System 2 planning. Table 5 is repeated here with its caveat that the cross-model comparison measures serialization rather than matched latency. The section also contains statements on AI use, ethics, reproducibility, and institutional scope. The ethics statement says driving was evaluated offline on nuScenes and manipulation in simulation, with no real-world deployment.
sections.heading: Conclusion
sections.headline: Conclusion argues that precise perception suits fast execution while broad reasoning models handle planning.

sections.body: The appendix gives the input/output protocol, with a coordinate vocabulary of 1,000 tokens, and the prompts for each task. It lists the architecture: a 27-layer vision encoder and a 36-layer language backbone. The complete model has approximately 4.844B parameters, and the tokenizer extends the base vocabulary to 152,670 entries. The data engine section describes field-level fusion, task-dependent validation, and targeted observations for expert iteration. Training has four supervised stages plus reinforcement learning, and the appendix reports aggregate training exposure in tokens across the pretraining phases. Stage 4 uses cross-entropy on coordinates and adds no separate IoU regression loss. Figures 12 to 21 give qualitative examples and state that they are not additional accuracy or recall estimates.
sections.heading: Appendix
sections.headline: Appendix covers the protocol, architecture, data engine, training stages, and qualitative grounding examples.
